links.outcome: ML exacerbation prediction performance by user engagement level (data sparsity)
links.effect: Performance was better for the most engaged users; the decrease for less frequent users was mostly offset when they engaged more near exacerbation. 60.3% engage frequently; 18.4% show transitional engagement.
links.quote: Machine learning performed better for users who engaged the most, however, this performance decrease can be mostly offset for less frequent users who engage more near exacerbation.

unlisted_practices: Encouraging users to self-report when they notice changes in their condition, rather than only at clinically defined symptoms, to keep data predictive while limiting disengagement from self-reporting burden

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating real-world patient engagement with an mHealth app (myCOPD) and its impact on predictive risk model performance for COPD exacerbations, supplemented with qualitative interviews.
